Grandiloquence

/gran-DIL-uh-kwens/ - the stress falls on DIL · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Grandiloquence means lofty, pompous language.

The menu's grandiloquence was legendary: a grilled cheese arrived as 'artisanal hearth-kissed curds embraced by heritage grain.'

Worked Example

The debate coach let the freshman finish his opening — 'we stand at the fulcrum of history's eternal pendulum' — then circled one word on her clipboard: grandiloquence. 'The judges,' she said, 'award points for arguments. Give them one plain sentence with a fact in it.'

Grandiloquence is language dressed above its station: lofty, pompous wording chosen to sound magnificent rather than to say something. Eloquence moves an audience; grandiloquence performs for it, and listeners usually hear the difference within a sentence.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

bombast: noisy, inflated language — grandiloquence's blustery twin

pomposity: self-importance in manner or speech; grandiloquence is pomposity's vocabulary

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

plainness: saying the thing in the words it needs, no costume

directness: aiming straight at the point without ornament

Where it sits · how far ornament swamps the meaning — polish → floweriness → grandiloquence

polish vs. grandiloquence: Polish is simply care — smooth sentences, good rhythm; it stops far short of grandiloquence and usually improves a speech.

floweriness vs. grandiloquence: Floweriness goes further than polish, draping blossoms of ornament over every noun, but grandiloquence tops this ladder: the ornament turns pompous and the meaning disappears under it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — grandi

Root — grandi: great (Latin grandis)

Root — loqu

Root — loqu: to speak (Latin loqui)

Suffix — ence

Suffix — ence: noun ending: a state or quality

Put it together

Put it together: Latin grandis ('great') plus loqui ('to speak') builds grandiloquence: literally 'grand-speaking.' The root loqu- chatters through English — a soliloquy is speaking alone, a ventriloquist throws speech — but here the grandeur is the problem: talk puffed up to sound greater than its matter.

Use the root in a new word: soliloquy

Use the root in a new word: soliloquy: Alone on the darkened stage, the prince begins his soliloquy, thinking out loud with no one to hear.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / critical

Grandiloquence is a critic's word — you diagnose it in someone else's inflated speech. Bombast stresses noise, pomposity stresses self-importance, and turgid, this unit's adjective for swollen prose, describes the style itself; grandiloquence names the lofty wording. None of them are compliments.
